strings.text: Licensing is the other axis
strings.original: Licensing is the other axis

strings.text: A trust class says what a host can see. A licence class says what a customer can do with the code. CARLOS doesn't dictate: you choose.
strings.original: A trust class says what a host can see. A licence class says what a customer can do with the code. CARLOS dictates neither; it asks you to name both.

strings.text: Libre
strings.original: Libre

strings.text: Free as in freedom and free of charge. Anyone may run, change and redistribute it. The operator earns from hosting or support, or not at all.
strings.original: Free as in freedom and free of charge. Anyone may run, change and redistribute it. The operator earns from hosting or support, or not at all.

strings.text: Source-available, commercial

strings.text: You can read it and self-host it; commercial use or redistribution needs a licence from the author.

strings.text: Fully open, and the author also runs it for you. The hosted service is the product; the code is the guarantee you can leave.

strings.text: Closed source, hosted only
strings.original: Closed source, hosted only

strings.text: The author runs it and does not ship the code. Ownership for the customer means their instance, their data and their trust class, not the software.
strings.original: The author runs it and does not ship the code. Ownership for the customer means their instance, their data and their trust class, not the binary.

strings.text: Closed source, hosted and on-prem
strings.original: Closed source, hosted and on-prem

strings.text: The author ships a binary the customer may run on their own boxes under licence, and also hosts it. One codebase, every deployment mode. Like status-quo SaaS, but better.
strings.original: The author ships a binary the customer may run on their own boxes under licence, and also hosts it. One codebase, every deployment mode.

strings.text: The two axes are independent. An L5 app can be class A; an L1 app can be class C. A gallery entry names both, or says which has not been published yet.

strings.text: Remixability is the third
strings.original: Remixability is the third

strings.text: Trust says what a host can see. Licence says what a customer may do. Remixability says what an agent, or a person with a fork, _can_ actually do today. Three flags, each yes or no.
strings.original: Trust says what a host can see. Licence says what a customer may do. Remixability says what an agent, or a person with a fork, can actually do today. Three flags, each yes or no.

strings.text: Forkable
strings.original: Forkable

strings.text: The source is available and a fork that stays close to upstream keeps working with the shared glue: sign-on, the edge, hibernation, the trust class, push notifications, integrations. Drift far enough and you are on your own, which is fair.
strings.original: The source is available and a fork that stays close to upstream keeps working with the shared glue: sign-on, the edge, hibernation, the trust class. Drift far enough and you are on your own, which is fair.

strings.text: Agent-driveable
strings.original: Agent-driveable

strings.text: The app opts actions in as typed tools, so an agent reaches the same handler a person does, through the same middleware, with a confirmation sentence on every write. The framework provides this; the app has to switch it on.
strings.original: The app opts actions in as typed tools, so an agent reaches the same handler a person does, through the same middleware, with a confirmation sentence on every write. The framework provides this; the app has to switch it on.

strings.text: Agent-rebuildable
strings.original: Agent-rebuildable

strings.text: The app publishes a skill at its well-known URL, so an agent can fork it, change it and redeploy it without a person reading the code first. The framework publishes two skills; each app owes its own.
strings.original: The app publishes a skill at its well-known URL, so an agent can fork it, change it and redeploy it without a person reading the code first. The framework publishes two skills; each app owes its own.

strings.text: All three are possible for every app in the family, because every app has the same shape. The gallery records which ones have done it, not which ones could.
strings.original: All three are possible for every app in the family, because every app has the same shape. The gallery records which ones have done it, not which ones could.

strings.text: Every app carries a trust class, S to C, a licence class, L1 to L5, and three remix flags. Publish the database and see what leaks.
